All statements other than statements of historical facts contained in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q, including statements regarding our future results of operations or financial condition, business strategy and plans and objectives of management for future operations, are forward-looking statements. In some cases, you can identify forward-looking statements because they contain words such as “anticipate,” “believe,” “contemplate,” “continue,” “could,” “estimate,” “expect,” “intend,” “may,” “plan,” “potential,” “predict,” “project,” “should,” “target,” “will” or “would” or the negative of these words or other similar terms or expressions. Forward-looking statements contained in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q include, but are not limited to, statements about: our future financial performance, including our revenue, cost of revenue, gross profit, and operating expenses; trends in our key business metrics; our ability to successfully retain and expand usage of our existing customers and attract new customers; the amount of remaining performance obligations that we expect to recognize as revenue over future periods; our growth and product strategy for our agentic inference cloud platform; our ability to operate our business and effectively manage our scale under evolving macroeconomic conditions, such as geopolitical conflicts, tariffs and trade tensions, inflationary pressures, interest rate fluctuations, and foreign currency exchange rate volatility; our ability to effectively manage our growth and future expenses; the sufficiency of our cash and cash equivalents, cash flow from operations and availability under our credit facility to meet our liquidity needs; and other statements regarding our future operations, financial condition, and prospects and business strategies.

The Company has performance obligations associated with commitments in customer contracts for future services that have not yet been recognized in the condensed consolidated financial statements. As of September 30, 2026, the aggregate transaction price allocated to the remaining performance obligations, which includes contracts with expected term of one year or less, was $799,707 with a weighted-average life of 3.7 years. As of September 30, 2026, the Company expects to recognize $345,111 of its remaining performance obligations as revenue over the next 12 months, with the remainder recognized thereafter over the remaining life of the contracts.

On May 5, 2025, the Company entered into a credit agreement (the “Credit Agreement”) by and among the Company, its wholly owned subsidiary, DigitalOcean, LLC, as borrower, Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc., as administrative agent, and the other parties thereto for a $500,000 senior secured delayed draw term loan facility (“Term Loan Facility”, and any loans thereunder “Term Loans”) and a $300,000 senior secured revolving credit facility (“Revolving Facility”, and any loans thereunder “Revolving Loans”) which includes a $30,000 sublimit for the issuance of letters of credit (collectively the “2025 Credit Facility”). On May 4, 2026, the Company entered into an amendment to the Credit Agreement (the “First Amendment”), which, among other modifications, (i) increased the Revolving Facility to $412,500, (ii) increased the letter of credit sublimit to $80,000, and (iii) amended the definition of “Indebtedness” to provide that capitalized leases shall be deemed to be an amount equal to 25% of the capitalized amount. The Term Loan Facility and Revolving Facility mature on May 5, 2030, and are subject to a springing maturity date in the event certain conditions occur as described in the Credit Agreement. Revolving Loans may be borrowed, repaid and reborrowed, until their maturity date. Term Loans may be borrowed until February 5, 2026 and, once borrowed and repaid, cannot be reborrowed.

On February 3, 2026, the Company drew down the remaining $120,000 available principal under its Term Loan Facility resulting in a total outstanding principal amount of $500,000. On March 27, 2026, the Company repaid the $500,000 outstanding principal of its Term Loan Facility in cash from the proceeds of its follow-on offering (see Note 11. Stockholders’ Equity) and wrote-off $2,700 of related unamortized issuance cost as loss on extinguishment of debt in other (expense) income, net on the Company’s condensed consolidated statements of operations during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

The Credit Agreement includes customary representations, warranties, and affirmative and negative covenants, including financial covenants that require the Company to maintain certain levels of total net leverage ratio and interest coverage ratio. As of September 30, 2026, the Company was in compliance with all covenants under the 2025 Credit Facility.

The Company was issued letters of credit under the letter of credit sublimit of its Revolving Facility of $9,734 and $15,584 during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively. No drawdowns have been made under the Company’s letters of credit and the Revolving Facility. The Company’s total available borrowing capacity under the Revolving Facility was $396,916 as of September 30, 2026.

On September 10, 2026, the Company and its wholly owned subsidiary, DigitalOcean, LLC (the “Lessee”), entered into an agreement with MUFG Americas Capital Leasing & Finance, LLC, as lessor (the “Lessor”), MUFG Bank, Ltd., as administrative agent and collateral agent, and the other parties thereto providing for up to $725,000 of committed financing to fund purchases of data center equipment, including an accordion feature permitting the Company to increase the committed financing by up to an additional $300,000 to $1,025,000 in the aggregate (the “Equipment Lease Facility”). The Company may request advances through September 10, 2027, funding up to 90% of the cost of equipment with the Lessee funding the remaining balance as prepaid rent, and the Lessor will acquire equipment with such funds and lease it to the Lessee. The Equipment Lease Facility matures on September 10, 2030. Each advance drawn under the Equipment Lease Facility will be accounted for as a separate finance lease.

Rent under each equipment lease is payable monthly in arrears and amortizes the applicable advance in full by September 10, 2030. Each equipment lease bears interest at a fixed rate, determined at the time of the applicable drawdown, equal to a term SOFR swap rate plus 2.75% per annum. Undrawn commitments under the Equipment Lease Facility are subject to a commitment fee of 0.20% per annum, increasing to 0.40% per annum six months after closing. The Lessee may prepay and purchase the equipment in whole or in part, subject to a prepayment premium of 5% in the first year and 3% in the second year following the applicable advance. Title to the equipment will transfer to the Lessee for nominal consideration upon payment in full of the amounts under the applicable equipment lease.

In connection with the Equipment Lease Facility, the Company paid customary arrangement, upfront and agency fees of $7,274, which are recognized as deferred financing fees in other assets within the condensed consolidated balance sheets, and are deferred until drawdown and will be amortized through the Equipment Lease Facility maturity on September 10, 2030. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had not drawn advances under the Equipment Lease Facility. The Company’s total available borrowing capacity under the Equipment Lease Facility was $725,000 as of September 30, 2026.

In relation to the execution of data center leases, the Company was issued letters of credit under the letter of credit sublimit of its Revolving Facility of $9,734 and $15,584 during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively. There were no outstanding letters of credit as of December 31, 2025. No drawdowns have been made under the Company’s letters of credit as of September 30, 2026. Refer to Note 7. Debt of the condensed consolidated financial statements for further details.

Other (expense) income, net consists primarily of induced conversion expense related to the partial repurchase of 2030 Convertible Notes, loss on extinguishment of our Term Loan Facility, cash interest expense on our Term Loan Facility, credit facilities, finance leases and equipment financing obligations, amortization of debt issuance costs, interest income on our money market funds, accretion of our marketable securities, and gains or losses on foreign currency exchange.

Other expense, net was $83.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to other income, net of $55.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The change was primarily due to induced conversion expense of $57.1 million related to the partial repurchase of our 2030 Convertible Notes, gain on partial extinguishment of our 2026 Convertible Notes of $48.1 million recognized in 2025, an increase of $24.9 million in interest expense primarily driven by interest on our finance leases and equipment financing arrangements, a decrease of $10.1 million in net unrealized gains related to foreign currency fluctuations from our operations, a loss of $2.7 million on the extinguishment of our Term Loan Facility, and an increase of $1.6 million in other expenses, net, partially offset by a $4.9 million increase in interest income due to higher investment balance from the proceeds of our public equity offering completed in March 2026 and accretion of our marketable securities.

We have funded our operations since inception primarily with cash flow generated by operations, offerings of our equity and debt securities, and borrowings under our credit facilities, equipment financing arrangements and finance leases. Cash provided from these sources is used primarily for operating expenses, such as personnel and co-location costs, capital expenditures, including our investments in AI/ML and other core product offerings, and principal repayments of finance leases and equipment financing obligations for servers and related equipment. From time to time, we may also use excess cash and/or debt for share repurchases and investments in marketable securities and cash equivalents.
In February 2026, we borrowed an additional $120.0 million under our Term Loan Facility.
Term Loan Facility during the three months ended March 31, 2026.

On May 4, 2026, we entered into an amendment to our Credit Agreement (the "First Amendment"). The First Amendment amends the Credit Agreement to, among other modifications, (i) provide for a $112.5 million increase in the Revolving Facility thereunder, (ii) provide for a $50.0 million increase in the letter of credit sublimit thereunder and (iii) amend the definition of “Indebtedness” to provide that capitalized leases shall be deemed to be an amount equal to 25% of the capitalized amount.

On September 10, 2026, we entered into an agreement with MUFG Americas Capital Leasing & Finance, LLC, as lessor, MUFG Bank, Ltd., as administrative agent and collateral agent, and the other parties thereto for up to $725.0 million of committed financing to fund purchases of data center equipment (the “Equipment Lease Facility”), including an accordion feature permitting us to increase the committed financing by up to an additional $300.0 million to $1,025.0 million in the aggregate (the “Equipment Lease Facility”). The Equipment Lease Facility matures on September 10, 2030 and we may request advances until September 10, 2027. As of September 30, 2026, we had not drawn advances under the Equipment Lease Facility. On October 6, 2026, we exercised an additional $60.0 million of the accordion feature, increasing the total committed financing to $785.0 million.

During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, we were issued letters of credit of $9.7 million and $15.6 million under the letter of credit sublimit of our Revolving Facility, respectively. For further information refer to Note 7. Debt in our condensed consolidated financial statements.

As of September 30, 2026, we had $666.1 million in cash and cash equivalents, $178.6 million in marketable securities, as well as $396.9 million of available borrowing capacity available under our Revolving Facility and $725 million of available commitments under our Equipment Lease Facility. On October 6, 2026, we exercised an additional $60.0 million of the accordion feature under our Equipment Lease Facility, increasing the total available borrowing capacity to $785.0 million. Our cash and cash equivalents primarily consist of cash and money market funds. Our marketable securities consist of U.S. Treasury securities and commercial paper. We believe our existing cash and cash equivalents, cash flow from operations and availability under our Revolving Facility and Equipment Lease Facility will be sufficient to support our requirements for working capital and capital expenditures, outstanding contractual commitments, debt and finance lease liabilities and equipment financing obligations both over the next 12 months and beyond.

Net cash used in investing activities was $382.0 million and $138.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The change was primarily driven by purchases of marketable securities of $177.6 million, a $14.9 million increase in cash payments for capital expenditures, an increase of $47.5 million in cash payments for the acquisition of equipment under financing arrangements (for which we received an equivalent amount of proceeds discussed below in “Financing Activities”), and a $4.0 million payment for acquisition of an AI-related business.

Net cash provided by financing activities was $475.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net cash used in financing activities of $307.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The change was primarily driven by proceeds of $1,473.9 million from our direct offering for induced conversion of 2030 Convertible Notes, proceeds of $887.9 million from our 2026 Follow-on Offering, $120.0 million drawdown on our Term Loan Facility and $75.1 million from equipment financing arrangements, partially offset by a $1,478.1 million settlement payment of the 2030 convertible senior notes, $500.0 million repayment of our Term Loan Facility, $62.1 million of payments of employee payroll taxes related to net share settlement of equity awards and $39.9 million of principal repayments for finance leases and financing arrangements for data center equipment.

We define non-GAAP net income as net income attributable to common stockholders, excluding stock-based compensation, acquisition related compensation, amortization of acquired intangibles, acquisition and integration related costs, restructuring and other charges, restructuring related charges, impairment of certain long-lived assets, (gain) loss on extinguishment of debt, net, induced conversion expense and other charges. In addition to these exclusions, we subtract an assumed non-GAAP provision for income taxes to calculate non-GAAP net income that excludes the current period income tax benefit (expense). We utilize a fixed long-term projected tax rate in our computation of the non-GAAP income tax provision in order to provide better consistency across reporting periods. We define non-GAAP diluted net income per share as non-GAAP net income divided by the weighted-average diluted shares outstanding, which includes the potentially dilutive effect of our stock options, RSUs, PRSUs, and Convertible Notes and, beginning in the first quarter of 2026, excludes the in-the-money portion of our 2030 Convertible Notes as they are covered by our capped call transactions, which are expected to mitigate the dilutive effect of our 2030 Convertible Notes.
